newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle end higher, set 41-month peak.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle end higher, set 41-month peak.

text.p: CME feeder cattle futures continued their recent strong advance, rising to the highest level for the nearby contract since February 1994.

"I think the driving force in the feeder market is still the corn price. Cattle feeders are seeing prices for corn they haven't seen in a long time," said analyst Joe Kropf of Joe Kropf and Sid Love Consulting.

Dealers said there was also growing talk about tight supplies with the U.S. Department of Agriculture's semi-annual cattle inventory report, to be issued Friday, expected to show a decline in the U.S. calf crop.
"We will be down again (following a two percent decline last year) and that means tighter supplies. The cash (feeder) market has stayed very strong," Kropf said.
The latest CME feeder index, for July 16, was up $0.23 per cwt at $81.70.

Corn prices on the Chicago Board of Trade last week fell to their lowest level since March 1995, and after a brief rally early this week the market has begun to show renewed signs of weakness, closing 2-3/4 to 1/4 cent lower on Thursday.
Floor sources said Cargill Investor Services was the biggest buyer of August feeders and also the major seller.
